title: Approximating Human Preferences Using a Multi-Judge Learned System

bias_targets.methodology: Progressively contaminating training data by replacing a fraction of simulated human preference scores with biased versions exhibiting systematic bias (consistent rating shifts), random noise, or scale compression (avoiding extreme scores) to evaluate the aggregator's resilience.

Applying mathematical transformations to individual LLM judge scores to simulate behavior patterns such as bottom-heavy (overly critical), top-heavy (overly generous), middle-heavy (avoiding extremes), and systematic positive/negative shifts to test robustness against rubric and prompt perturbations.
